questions.stem: A bag contains 4 red, 7 blue and 3 yellow marbles. One marble is picked at random. What is the probability of picking a red or yellow marble?
questions.explanation: Total marbles = 4 + 7 + 3 = 14. Red or yellow = 4 + 3 = 7. P(red or yellow) = 7/14 = 1/2. Options (a) and (c) are the same value; the simplified form is 1/2.

questions.stem: A standard deck has 52 cards. What is the probability of drawing a card that is a heart or a king?
questions.explanation: There are 13 hearts and 4 kings, but the king of hearts is counted in both groups. P = (13 + 4 − 1)/52 = 16/52 = 4/13. A common error is double-counting the king of hearts to get 17/52.

questions.stem: A letter is chosen at random from the word MATHEMATICS. What is the probability of choosing the letter A?
questions.explanation: MATHEMATICS has 11 letters: M-A-T-H-E-M-A-T-I-C-S. The letter A appears 2 times. P(A) = 2/11. A common error is counting only distinct letters (giving 1/8) or miscounting the total.

questions.stem: The probability of a biased coin landing on heads is 0.6. Sam flips the coin 200 times. How many times would you expect it to land on tails?
questions.explanation: P(tails) = 1 − 0.6 = 0.4. Expected tails = 200 × 0.4 = 80. A common error is calculating 200 × 0.6 = 120, which gives expected heads, not tails.

questions.stem: A box contains red and blue pens only. The probability of picking a red pen is 3/8. There are 12 red pens. How many blue pens are in the box?
questions.explanation: If P(red) = 3/8, then red/total = 3/8. With 12 red: 12/total = 3/8, so total = 32. Blue pens = 32 − 12 = 20. A common error is giving the total (32) instead of just the blue pens.
